title: Sort by a column the user picks, safely

blocks.text: Parameters carry **values**. The page's first best practice warns that they cannot carry identifiers or keywords: a user-chosen `ORDER BY` column or sort direction cannot be a `?`. Those parts must be **chosen from an allow-list of known names**, and anything else refused, never pasted into the SQL.
SELECT id, name, email FROM users ORDER BY <column> <DIRECTION>

items: `direction` is `asc` or `desc` in any case, written in upper case;

cases.says: name/asc, created_at/DESC and email/Desc give the query ending in ORDER BY name ASC, created_at DESC and email DESC; the column password is refused.
"name; DROP TABLE users", "name, (SELECT password FROM users)", "x_name" and "Name" are refused: the column must be exactly an allowed name.
"desc, (SELECT 1)", "descending", "asc " and null are refused as directions.

concepts: Parameterized queries carry values only; identifiers and keywords such as an ORDER BY column or direction are chosen from an allow-list.
